data_fields.name: turn_limit
data_fields.donor_constant: 170 units per step (DEGREES_30 of 2048 per turn, about 30 degrees)

data_fields.name: move_limit
data_fields.donor_constant: 128 map units per axis per step

data_fields.name: zoom_step_in
data_fields.donor_constant: x100/85 per step (integer division, at least +1)

data_fields.name: zoom_cap_while_controlled
data_fields.donor_constant: 30000 (above the normal max of 12000; do not copy)

data_fields.name: velocity_halving
data_fields.donor_constant: divide by 2 per camera step with no input

best_idea: A third-person follow camera can keep a focus point a fixed distance ahead of the hero, turn its yaw toward the hero's facing by a capped angle each tick, and move the focus by a capped distance each tick, so it never snaps.
decision_why: The per-turn clamped follow (turn limit to facing, per-axis move limit, zoom-in while controlled) is the shape the world camera needs; not adopt, because the donor is a top-down isometric grid camera with no wall test and no lateral shoulder offset, which the owner's over-the-shoulder camera needs.
acceptance: After a 180-degree turn of the hero in a world zone, the camera yaw reaches the hero's facing in a bounded number of steps, and a unit test asserts that no step changes yaw by more than the turn limit and no focus axis moves more than the move limit.
